messages.text:
"Create a 3D open-world survival/life-simulation game in first person (with a third-person option), set in a faithful version of Knoxville, Tennessee. The player is an ordinary person with no special powers, living day-to-day life in the city with total freedom.
1. World
Recognizable areas (downtown, Market Square, World's Fair Park, Old City, university campus, suburbs, the Tennessee River).
Day/night cycle, dynamic weather, NPCs with daily routines, traffic, and stores with opening hours.
Enterable interiors: houses, grocery stores, shops, gas stations, restaurants, junkyards, warehouses.
2. Free Collection
The player can pick up any interactable object: food, drinks, tools, clothes, electronics, furniture, materials, weapons, decorative items.
Items have weight, size, durability, and expiration (food spoils).
Items can be bought, found, traded, or looted.
3. Backpack and Inventory
Backpack with weight and space limits (grid-style inventory), with upgrades (bigger backpack, pockets, car trunk).
Visible gear on the character (backpack, clothes, holstered weapon).
Drag, stack, split, drop, and throw items.
4. Functional Phone
Realistic interface: calls, texts with NPCs, contacts, camera/gallery, GPS with a map of Knoxville, banking (money), online shop with delivery, clock/alarm, flashlight, notes, music.
Battery drains and needs a charger; signal varies by area.
Missions and events arrive via texts and calls.
5. Character Needs
Hunger, thirst, sleep, hygiene, health, and mood. Money and optional jobs (part-time work).
Cook, consume items, treat injuries with supplies.
6. Base and Decoration
The player chooses or buys a house, apartment, or abandoned building as a base.
Build/decoration system with free placement: move, rotate, scale, and anchor any item anywhere (walls, ceiling, floor, shelves), with physics and an optional snap grid.
Functional furniture (bed saves the game, fridge preserves food, chest stores items, workbench crafts).
Free-camera decoration mode, plus save and load layouts. Everything persists between sessions.
Optional defenses: reinforced doors, locks, cameras, traps.
7. Weapons and Combat
Melee, improvised, and firearms with ammo, reloading, maintenance, mods, and attachments.
Weapons can be displayed in the base or stored in a locker.
Realistic physics and consequences (police, reputation, injuries).
The player can avoid combat entirely and play peacefully.
8. Vehicles and Crafting
Car, motorcycle, and bicycle with fuel and storage.
Craft items from collected materials.
9. Progression and Freedom
No linear story: side missions, life routines, random events, reputation with NPCs.
Autosave and manual save.
10. Technical Requirements
Engine: [Unity / Unreal / Godot / Web with Three.js, pick one].
Deliver the folder structure, full code for each system (inventory, phone, building, combat, needs, save/load), run instructions, and a list of required assets.
Start with a minimum playable prototype: one city block, inventory, basic phone, and a base with decoration. Then expand in stages.
Before starting, list the development plan in phases and ask for confirmation.
"
